Confinement is a factory: makeConfineHook({ cwd, files, denials }) installed as hooks.PreToolUse[0].hooks[0], resolving deny for the four edit tools when path.relative(cwd, resolve(cwd, file_path)) starts '..' or is not in files, and {} otherwise.

One environment fact that shapes the default deps: @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk is NOT installed in this clone (no fleet/node_modules, no lockfile at BASE), so a static top-level import of it would make the module unimportable and every exam leg red. examiner (task 4, three role files): approach for fleet/tests/test_factory_roles.mjs, landing at fleet/tests/exams/run_185/test_factory_roles.mjs.

Plain node script in the house style of fleet/tests/test_resolver_brief.mjs — node:assert/strict, one labelled block per Proof leg, 'ALL TESTS PASSED' at the end. It only reads factory/roles/{implement,exam,resolve}.md through paths resolved from the file's own directory (four levels up to the repo root); it creates nothing, spawns nothing, and imports no module under test, so at BASE it goes red on leg (a)'s existence assertion — the three role files are not written yet.

Readings I am pinning, so a later session need not reconstruct them:
- (a) [M1] the sum is of the three PER-FILE whitespace-word counts, as the leg words it. That is >= the Proof's `cat ... | wc -w` by at most the count of files missing a trailing newline, so the leg's form is the stricter of the two and passing it passes the Run: line.
- (b) [M2] 'a sentence with X and Y' needs a sentence unit in markdown. I split on blank lines and on the start of a new block (list marker, heading, blockquote), then on terminal .!? — so a sentence wrapped across two lines stays one sentence, and two adjacent bullets do not merge into one.
- (b) [M2] 'contains the word `amendment`' is matched as lowercase/initial-capital whole word (amendment/amendments/Amendment), which is the leg's own typography and is a different word from the `AMENDMENTS:` section header the same clause already pins once.
- (b) [M2] 'a phrase with `not` and `create`' is encoded with `not` verbatim as the leg spells it, not widened to never/cannot.
- (d) [M4] line-level, and 'contains' is read as substring (so 'cannot' satisfies it); the trigger is the literal `git ` with its trailing space, as the leg spells it.

Approach, leg by leg, all six legs encoded as node:assert/strict in one linear script, red at BASE on the absent factory/worker.mjs:

- The deliverable is imported dynamically through pathToFileURL(ROOT/factory/worker.mjs) with ROOT resolved four levels up from the landing directory, guarded by a try/catch so BASE reports ABSENT MODULE as a named assertion rather than dying at load.
- (a) M1: fake deps.query yields system/init, three assistant messages (the middle one carrying a tool_use block, as the Context describes), one result; result deep-equals the last message, turns === 3, wall_ms a finite number. onMessage, which M1's signature names and the Context pins, is asserted to receive all five in order.
- (b) M2: options read off the one recorded query({ prompt, options }) argument; settingSources deep-equal [], permissionMode, cwd, systemPrompt, model, and disallowedTools containing each of the four literals.
- (c) M2: no schema -> the options carry no outputFormat key at all (the Context's ...(schema ? {} : {}) spread is the literal reading of 'carry no outputFormat'); with schema -> deep-equal { type: 'json_schema', schema }; mcpServers passed through by deep-equal.
- (d) M3: exactly one PreToolUse matcher with exactly one hook, invoked directly off the captured options with a single input object ({ tool_name, tool_input }) — the prototype's own hook shape. cwd is a real mkdtemp dir (realpath'd) with inside.txt on disk so an implementation that stats or realpaths still resolves. denials is read off the resolved call value and must be the live array M3 says the call answers.
- (e) M4: the fake iterator is gated so the run is genuinely in flight; startWorker answers handle, interruptWorker resolves 'ok' with interrupt called exactly once, then the gate opens and the promise resolves.
- (f) M5: newline count of factory/worker.mjs <= 200 (wc -l semantics), and fleet/package.json's dependencies['@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk'] a non-empty string.

The exam imports nothing from @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk and opens no socket: every call is through the injected deps.

payload.body:
Landed: factory/worker.mjs (139 lines) + the one dependency line in fleet/package.json. Both Run proofs green; all six exam legs green against a scratch probe driven from the run dir (never written into the tree), including the (d) matrix over Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit, the inside/escape/Read cases, and (e) interrupt-exactly-once.

Two decisions a later session would otherwise rediscover:

1. No fleet/package-lock.json in this diff. The task text says the lockfile is the worker's to regenerate with 'npm install' in fleet/, but (i) no lockfile exists at BASE, so there is nothing to regenerate; (ii) fleet/package-lock.json is not in the task's Files; (iii) fleet/sandbox-boot.sh:902 already falls back to 'npm install' when fleet/node_modules is missing and no lockfile exists, and run-waves.mjs drops lockfile basenames at capture and regenerates them at fold; (iv) node_modules/ is NOT in .gitignore, so running npm install in this clone would put the whole tree into the captured patch. Leaving the lockfile to the run's own regenerator is the safe reading.

2. The SDK default deps.query is loaded with a try/caught top-level dynamic import, not a static import, because @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk is not installed in the clones. A static import makes the module unimportable and every exam leg red; the caught import keeps 'deps defaults to { query } from the SDK' true at runtime and throws a named error only if a real dispatch is attempted with no SDK and no deps.query.

Also: startWorker attaches a no-op .catch() arm to the promise it returns (the caller still sees the rejection) so a handle-only caller — leg (e)'s fake, which interrupts and never awaits — cannot trip unhandledRejection in the exam process.

payload.author: impl:3@run-185
payload.body:
Task 3 (factory/tools.mjs). Approach: one named export `factoryTools({ kata, projectId, task, candidates })` returning `createSdkMcpServer({ name: 'factory', tools })` with four `tool()` defs (note, hand, settled, sibling_fact).

Probed the real SDK (0.3.275) in a scratch dir, since fleet/node_modules does not exist at BASE (Task 1 adds the dep; sandbox-boot.sh runs the install): `tool(name, desc, zodRawShape, handler)`, and `createSdkMcpServer` answers `{ type: 'sdk', name, instance }` whose `instance._registeredTools` is keyed by tool name with a `.handler` on each — so the exam's 'read through the instance's registered tool list' leg works natively. I also attach non-enumerable `tools`/`handlers` to the config so the exam can invoke handlers directly without touching an underscore-private.

Resolution detail worth keeping: a bare `import '@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk'` from factory/ does NOT resolve — node walks factory/ -> repo root, and the install lives at fleet/node_modules. The module therefore tries the bare specifier, then ../fleet/node_modules/... by path, then createRequire rooted at fleet/package.json, all under a top-level await so factoryTools itself stays synchronous.

The exam lands at `fleet/tests/exams/run_185/test_factory_judge.mjs` (EXAM PATHS), so `../../../../` is the repository root and `factory/judge.mjs` is imported through it; both JSON inputs are read from the root at test time, never inlined.

examiner, round 1 — the approach I am about to take.

The exam lands at `fleet/tests/exams/run_185/test_factory_tools.mjs` (EXAM PATHS), so every relative path in it is written for THAT directory: `../../../../` is the repository root, and the deliverable is imported as `../../../../factory/tools.mjs`.

How the four tools are reached. Leg (a) offers two readings — "the instance's registered tool list, or the config's tool handlers exported for the exam". I take the FIRST, because it needs no export beyond the one `Produces:` names. Measured against @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.3.275 in a scratch install: `createSdkMcpServer({name, version, tools})` answers `{ type: 'sdk', name, instance }`, and `instance._registeredTools` is a name -> definition map whose entries carry the user's own function under `handler`; `handler(args, extra)` answers the `{content:[{type:'text',text}]}` the handler returned, verbatim. The exam reads that map (falling back to `registeredTools`, and to `callback` for the older MCP spelling) so an SDK version bump is not mistaken for a missing tool. It imports the SDK itself nowhere — resolution from `factory/` is the implementer's problem, not the exam's.

The legs, and what each becomes. (a) `name === 'factory'` and the sorted tool names deep-equal `['hand','note','settled','sibling_fact']`; `type === 'sdk'` is asked once under [M1] as the part of "returns the value of createSdkMcpServer" no leg asks. (b) one `comment` call with args deep-equal `['p','u','hi']` and an answer naming the uid the fake returned; one `patchMetadata` whose patch deep-equals the two dotted keys flat — a nested `{work:{attention}}` fails that equality, which is CONTRACT.md's `metadata-dotted-flat` row held live. (c) the settled patch's keys are exactly `['interface.settled']`, its value is a STRING, and `JSON.parse` of it deep-equals `{symbol,file,task:'1'}`; the refusal makes zero kata calls. (d) one `getIssue('s')`, the answer's JSON deep-equals the fake issue's `metadata`; with the fake rejecting, the invocation RESOLVES and its text begins `no fact:`. (e) the newline count of `factory/tools.mjs` is at most 200 — newlines, not split-length, so the exam counts exactly what the Run's `wc -l` counts.

Three readings a later session would otherwise reconstruct. (1) `patchMetadata` is pinned on projectId, uid and patch and NOT on a fourth `revision` argument: the leg says "whose patch is deep-equal to", and the client's signature carries an optional revision, so pinning arity would grade a choice the Proof does not make. (2) M3 says the refusal names "every candidate name" while leg (c) names only `catalog`; leg (c) is written with the single candidate it spells, and the plural is asked once more under [M3] with three candidates, so "every" is measured without reshaping the leg. (3) `factoryTools` is called SYNCHRONOUSLY — `Produces:` is `-> McpSdkServerConfigWithInstance`, not a promise of one — so an async implementation fails leg (a) rather than being quietly awaited.

Red at BASE for one reason: `factory/tools.mjs` does not exist, so the dynamic import fails and the first assertion names it as the absent deliverable. The import is dynamic precisely so BASE reports that assertion rather than dying at load.
